extraction.name: LAMBADA
extraction.description: LAMBADA is a dataset to evaluate the capabilities of computational models for text understanding by means of a word prediction task. It is a collection of narrative passages sharing the characteristic that human subjects are able to guess their last word if they are exposed to the whole passage, but not if they only see the last sentence preceding the target word.
extraction.creator: Denis Paperno, German Kruszewski, Angeliki Lazaridou, Quan Ngoc Pham, Raffaella Bernardi, Sandro Pezzelle, Marco Baroni, Gemma Boleda, Raquel Fernandez
extraction.citeAs: Paperno, D., Kruszewski, G., Lazaridou, A., Pham, Q. N., Bernardi, R., Pezzelle, S., Baroni, M., Boleda, G., & Fernandez, R. (2016). The LAMBADA dataset: Word prediction requiring a broad discourse context. arXiv preprint arXiv:1606.06031.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The LAMBADA data come from the Book Corpus. The novels were randomly divided into equally-sized training and development+testing partitions. Passages were extracted, filtered by automated language models to remove easy instances, and then evaluated by human subjects through the CrowdFlower crowdsourcing service in a three-step guessing process.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data comes from the Book Corpus (Zhu et al., 2015), which contains unpublished novels.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Duplicate removal and filtering out of potentially offensive material with a stop word list. Passages that were relatively easy for standard language models were filtered out (any passage whose target word had probability >= 0.00175 according to any of four baseline language models was excluded).
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human subjects evaluated passages in three steps: 1) One subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage. 2) If correct, a second subject guessed the target word based on the whole passage. 3) If also correct, up to 10 subjects tried to guess the target word based on the target sentence only (allowed 3 guesses each). If no subject could guess it from the sentence alone, the passage was added to the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A strict hit-or-miss approach was used, keeping only items that could be unambiguously determined by human subjects. The protocol required two consecutive subjects to exactly match the missing word in broad context, and ensured that no subject (out of ten) was able to provide it based on local context only.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Four language models (a pre-trained RNN, a standard 4-gram model, a RNN, and a feed-forward model) were used for automated filtering prior to human annotation.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Proper nouns are hugely overrepresented in LAMBADA (48%), while verbs, adjectives, and adverbs are under-represented compared to the POS distribution in the input. LAMBADA items also contain quoted direct speech significantly more often than the input items overall.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Standard language models are bound to fail on it by design, as one of the first filters was to choose passages where a number of simple language models failed to predict the upcoming word.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Testing language models on their ability to take a broad discourse context into account when predicting a word. It is meant to encourage the development of new models capable of genuine understanding of broad context in natural language text.
